Work items, git repositories and pull requests on Azure DevOps Services (dev.azure.com)

skills/toil/ado-cloud.md

Work items, git repositories and pull requests on Azure DevOps Services (https://dev.azure.com/<organization>, or the older https://<organization>.visualstudio.com), through its REST API with api-version=7.1. Built from Microsoft’s REST API reference and never run against a live organization. Verification level: unit.

For Azure DevOps Server (on-premises), use the ado area instead. The two are separate areas so that neither one’s fixes can change the other: a Services connection is one organization, where a Server connection is a server holding several collections.

Supported versions: The oldest Azure DevOps Services version toil supports hasn’t been established. Azure DevOps Services is always current. toil sends api-version=7.1, the newest released version (7.2 is preview only), with 7.1-preview.1 for connection data and 7.1-preview.4 for work item comments, which exist only as previews.

Credential

An organization-scoped personal access token: in Azure DevOps, User settings → Personal access tokens → New Token, with Organization set to the one organization this connection is for. Give it the scopes the commands you’ll use need: Work Items and Code, Read (or Read & write for the write commands), plus Project and Team Read for project list. toil sends it as Authorization: Basic base64(":" + token), with an empty user name.

Don’t create a global token (“All accessible organizations”). Microsoft is retiring global personal access tokens: every existing one stops working on December 1, 2026. A connection is one organization, so an organization-scoped token is all it needs. A 401 or 403 is AUTH, and its fix says to create an organization-scoped token and that global ones are being retired.

There is no OAuth, Microsoft Entra ID or service principal sign-in: those need a browser login or an app registration, and toil takes only a token you create once.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_ADO_CLOUD_BASE_URLyesOrganization URL: https://dev.azure.com/<organization> (or https://<organization>.visualstudio.com)
patTOIL_ADO_CLOUD_PATyesOrganization-scoped personal access token (a secret)
projectTOIL_ADO_CLOUD_PROJECTnoDefault project, when --project isn’t given
repoTOIL_ADO_CLOUD_REPOnoDefault git repository, when --repo isn’t given
fieldAliasesTOIL_ADO_CLOUD_FIELD_ALIASESnoWork item field aliases as a JSON object, friendly name to reference name, e.g. {"effortdays": "MyOrg.EffortDays"}
writesTOIL_ADO_CLOUD_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

A baseUrl that doesn’t name exactly one organization is refused with CONFIG_INVALID before anything is sent: https://dev.azure.com with no organization or with more after it (a project), or a visualstudio.com URL with any path other than the legacy /DefaultCollection.

export TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_BASE_URL=https://dev.azure.com/imagile
export TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_PAT=<your organization-scoped token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with project and repo usually set once under defaults.ado-cloud:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "imagile-ado": { "area": "ado-cloud", "baseUrl": "https://dev.azure.com/imagile", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "ado-cloud": { "connection": "imagile-ado", "project": "Imagile", "repo": "imagile-api" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add imagile-ado --area ado-cloud (or toil connections login imagile-ado) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_PAT. Env vars always win over the file. For a second organization, add a second connection with its own token.

In Azure Pipelines, map the job’s own token and organization URL into the step:

- script: toil ado-cloud work get --id 42
  env:
    TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_PAT: $(System.AccessToken)
    TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_BASE_URL: $(System.CollectionUri)

ado-cloud doesn’t read SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN or SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI on its own. Azure Pipelines sets both under the same names on Server and on Services, and the ado area already takes SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, so if both areas read them, one job’s token would configure both. The job token has to be mapped into the step’s environment anyway, so naming it TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_PAT costs nothing. On Services, System.CollectionUri is the organization URL with a trailing slash (https://dev.azure.com/imagile/), which baseUrl accepts.

Where a command acts

--project <name> and --repo <name> are group flags, accepted before or after the command (toil ado-cloud --project Imagile work search --wiql ...). Without them, toil uses a dossier, then the connection’s project and repo. The git remote isn’t read. Over MCP they’re the project and repo fields. meta.context says where each came from.

  • A work item belongs to the organization, so work get, work update, work revisions and work get-batch need neither.
  • work create, work search, work list-comments, work add-comment, work list-iterations and repo list need a project.
  • Every other repo command needs a project and a repo.
  • whoami, project list and project get need neither.

Commands

Every command also takes --connection <name>. Write commands (marked ✎) need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. Names and flags match ado wherever the operation is the same. MCP tools are ado_cloud_<command> (ado_cloud_work_get). There are no deletes.

CommandFlagsReturns

Paging

project list, repo list-prs, work search, work revisions and work list-comments return the whole list by default. With --limit <n> they return at most that many and set meta.page.nextCursor; pass it back as --cursor, with the same --limit, for the next page, until it’s null. Every list except work search reads page by page (continuation tokens for projects and comments, $top and $skip for pull requests and revisions) and stops with an HTTP error after 1,000 pages, naming the list.

Work items

  • Fields. --field name=value takes a reference name (Microsoft.VSTS.Scheduling.StoryPoints=5) or an alias, matched ignoring case, spaces and dashes: the connection’s fieldAliases first, then the built-in ones (title, state, assignedto, description, areapath, iterationpath, iteration, tags, priority, severity, effort, storypoints, remainingwork, remaining, acceptancecriteria, reprosteps). Anything else is sent as given. Values are sent as text; the server converts them.
  • work update --rev <n> adds a JSON Patch test of the revision first, so the server refuses the whole change if someone else changed the item since you read it.
  • work search returns the matching ids and urls, not their fields; fetch those with work get-batch. --updated-since <iso> keeps only items changed at or after that instant: a date (2026-10-01, UTC midnight) or a date-time with its zone (2026-10-01T09:00:00Z). toil ANDs [System.ChangedDate] >= '<instant>' onto the query’s own WHERE, in parentheses so an OR keeps its meaning, and asks for time precision. Time precision applies to the whole query, so with --updated-since an = on a date field matches one exact instant, not a day; write date conditions with >= and < instead. It and --limit work on flat queries (FROM WorkItems) only; a link query is refused. With --limit, each page runs the query again, so an item changed in between can move. A query returns at most 20,000 items.
  • work get-batch --id <n> --id <n> reads 200 ids per request, at most 1,000 per call. value holds the items found in the order asked, with every field and relation, or only --fields; missing lists each id that doesn’t exist or the token can’t see, with an ADO_CLOUD_WORK_ITEMS_MISSING warning.
  • work revisions returns each revision as the whole item as it stood after that change, oldest first, so neighbours show what changed and when.

Pull requests

  • Branch names get refs/heads/; a full ref (refs/heads/x, refs/tags/x) is sent as given. --reviewers and --creator / --reviewer take identity ids (from whoami, or a pull request’s reviewers[].id), not names or emails.
  • --created-after and --created-before take a date (UTC midnight) or a date-time with its zone, as --updated-since does.
  • merge-pr reads the pull request for its source commit, then asks the server to complete it with --strategy noFastForward (default), squash, rebase or rebaseMerge. A pull request with no source commit yet is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is changed. Completion is asynchronous: check data.status and data.mergeStatus, which stay active and queued while policies or conflicts hold it.
  • update-pr doesn’t change reviewers: the API doesn’t take them on that call.
  • repo list-comments flattens every live thread’s comments, oldest first, each with threadId and threadContext (null for a general comment). System comments (votes, pushes) are left out unless --include-system. repo list-threads returns the threads themselves, system ones included.
  • repo add-inline-comment anchors on the right (new) side of --line unless --line-type left; a path without a leading / gets one.
  • repo resolve-comment sets --status fixed (resolved) by default; wontFix, closed, byDesign, pending, or active to reopen.

Output, compared with ado

data is the server’s own JSON, so where Services and Server agree it has the same shape as ado’s, and toil util owi map reads work get, work get-batch, work revisions and work list-iterations output from either area into Open Work Items. The differences, for anything that reads both:

  • Work items (work get, work get-batch, work revisions, work search) have the same shape: id, rev, fields keyed by reference name, relations, url. On Services every url is under the organization (https://dev.azure.com/<org>/_apis/...) with no collection segment. work get-batch returns { count, value, missing }, the same as ado’s.
  • Identities (System.AssignedTo, System.CreatedBy, createdBy, reviewers) are the same object, { displayName, id, uniqueName, url, imageUrl, descriptor }, but on Services uniqueName is the user’s sign-in email, descriptor starts with aad. (or msa.), and url is on vssps.dev.azure.com. On Server uniqueName is often DOMAIN\user.
  • work list-comments returns every comment, following continuation tokens; ado’s returns only the server’s first page. Each comment has the same shape.
  • work create takes --type, --title and the other flags, and --field; it has no --input-file or --parent, which ado’s has.
  • work update takes --field (and --rev); it has no --input-file.
  • repo list-comments leaves system comments out unless --include-system; ado’s includes them.
  • Ids are whole numbers, checked by the schema: --id 12abc is refused, where ado reads it as 12.

Any endpoint: ado-cloud api

When no command above covers an endpoint, ado-cloud api calls it directly. It sends the connection’s own token, the same way every other ado-cloud command does, to a path under the organization URL. Add api-version yourself:

toil ado-cloud api GET _apis/projects --query api-version=7.1
toil ado-cloud api GET Imagile/_apis/wit/workitemtypes --query api-version=7.1 --query '$expand=states'
toil ado-cloud api PATCH _apis/wit/workitems/42 --query api-version=7.1 --body-file patch.json --content-type application/json-patch+json --allow-write
  • The path is relative to baseUrl, with or without a leading / (in Git Bash on Windows, leave it off: the shell rewrites /_apis/... into a file path, which is refused). A full URL, a scheme, //host, a leading backslash or a . / .. segment is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent, so the token never leaves the connection’s host.
  • The method decides the gate. GET and HEAD are reads. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are writes: they need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. DELETE works only on the CLI: over MCP, ado_cloud_api refuses it with INVALID_INPUT.
  • --query key=value adds a query parameter; repeat it for more, or to repeat a key. --body-file <path> sends that file (inside the workspace, or - for stdin) as the body, as application/json unless --content-type says otherwise. A work item change is application/json-patch+json.
  • Output: a JSON body is data, parsed. A text body (text/*, XML, or no content type) is data as text. Any other body is binary: data is its bytes as base64, with an API_BINARY warning. Text and binary are capped at 1 MB, with an API_TRUNCATED warning when the body was longer. An empty body (a 204, a HEAD) is null. meta.response is { status, contentType }. Errors use the usual codes (AUTH, NOT_FOUND, HTTP, NETWORK) with Azure DevOps’s own message. A body labelled JSON that doesn’t parse comes back as text, with an API_NOT_JSON warning.
  • Over MCP it’s the ado_cloud_api tool, with method, path, query (an array of key=value strings), bodyFile, contentType and allowWrite.

Prefer a wrapped command when one exists: it knows the endpoint’s paging and quirks, and ado-cloud api doesn’t.

Notes

  • toil connections test reads the organization’s connection data, which names the token’s own user.
  • A 429 is retried after the delay Azure DevOps asks for, as in every area.
  • Not covered yet: pipelines and builds, attachments, work item types, states and fields, areas, links, tags, and PR files and diffs. ado-cloud api reaches all of them.

    TOIL_ADO_CLOUD_FIELD_ALIASES
